tasks.title: Give the character arms and legs that move
tasks.goal: The character is one sprite with squash/stretch and a bob. The user asked whether the arms and legs move - they do not. Add procedural limbs that run while grounded and hold a pose in the air, driven from the existing RunnerCharacterMotion so no new Update loop is introduced.
acceptance: Limbs are child GameObjects created at runtime by this component - do NOT change PrefabGenerator, and do not require any new art file.

In the air they stop cycling and hold a jump pose, and they return to the run cycle on landing.

Sorting: a SpriteRenderer child needs a lower sortingOrder than the body to draw behind it.
Keep it subtle. This is a 136x192 sprite on a phone; limbs that swing far read as broken, not lively.

tasks.title: Gemini design adapter (free tier only, never escalates)
tasks.goal: Add company/orchestrator/gemini_client.py so design work can be requested from Gemini's free tier. Model it on the two adapters already in this repo - ollama_client.py and codex_runner.py - which enforce their cost rules in code rather than in prose. Text prompts return text; image prompts return PNG bytes the caller writes under AI_GAME_COMPANY/generated/.
acceptance: Reads the API key ONLY from the env var named by policy gemini_api_key_env (GEMINI_API_KEY). Never from GOOGLE_API_KEY, which stays on blocked_env_keys, and never from a file in the repo.

The key value is never logged, printed, put in an exception message, or written to disk. A status helper may report that a key is PRESENT or ABSENT and nothing more - copy the 'names only' idiom from CodexRunner.stripped_keys.
Raises a PolicyViolation (from company.orchestrator.policy) before any network call when policy allow_gemini_design is not true. Test that no request is attempted in that case.
Refuses any model id that is not in the policy's gemini_free_tier_models list, with its own exception type. This is the free-tier gate and it must be checked before the request, not after.

On HTTP 429 or a quota/rate-limit response, raises a GeminiLimited exception - the same 'degrade, never spend' shape as CodexLimited. It must NOT retry against another model, another tier, or a billed project.

An HTTP error, an empty response, or a response that is not the expected content type raises rather than returning something falsy. A generation that did not happen is never reported as a generation that produced nothing.
Uses only the Python standard library (urllib.request). Do not add a dependency - google-generativeai is not installed and must not be added.
Network calls are injectable so the tests need no key and no network: follow the 'runner' test seam CodexRunner uses.
Tests cover: the policy gate, the free-model gate, key absence, a 429 degrading, a malformed response raising, and that the key never appears in any exception text or status string.
notes: Endpoint shape, verified from this container on 2026-09-02: GET https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED with 'Please use API Key' when unauthenticated - so the host is reachable and only the key is missing. Use that same host.

Google's own pricing/rate-limit page (ai.google.dev) is BLOCKED by this environment's egress proxy, so the free tier could not be confirmed from a first-party source. Do not write a comment claiming specific free quotas. Write the code so that exceeding quota fails loudly instead.
Do NOT call the API during the tests. There is no key here and a test that needs one is a test that never runs.
Login/key setup is a HUMAN_GATE (initial_gemini_login in company_policy.json). Report it, never perform it.

2026-09-02 RUN: done and committed as e1ade1b, in the same commit as CODEX-OFFICE1 and CODEX-OLLAMA1. Status set BY HAND for the same reason - the codex_runner bug left the board stale. Verified from the commit: the key is read only through the env var named by policy gemini_api_key_env, key_status reports PRESENT/ABSENT and never a value, allow_gemini_design raises PolicyViolation before any request, a model outside gemini_free_tier_models raises GeminiModelNotAllowed, 429 raises GeminiLimited with no retry against another model or tier, and the transport is injectable urllib with no new dependency. test_gemini_client.py: 17 tests, all pass. REVIEW, not DONE - no key exists yet (initial_gemini_login is still an open HUMAN_GATE), so not one line of this has spoken to Google. tasks.title: ParallaxBackground so the level can have background art
tasks.goal: The level has no background art at all - just a generated sky gradient. The approved kenney-background-elements-remastered pack cannot be used because nothing scrolls a background layer yet. Add that component so the art becomes a file copy afterwards.
acceptance: One MonoBehaviour that scrolls N background layers horizontally at per-layer speed factors, so distant layers move slower than near ones.
Structural wiring goes in a SetReferences/SetLayers method called at edit time; numeric tuning goes in a Configure method called at runtime. That split is a project rule, see CLAUDE.md.
Layers repeat seamlessly: when a layer has scrolled one full sprite width it wraps, with no visible gap or jump.
No allocation per frame - no GetComponent, no Find, no new objects in Update.
It works with NO layers assigned (does nothing, logs nothing) so a generated scene without background art is unaffected.
Runtime script: it must NOT reference UnityEditor in any form, or the Android build breaks.
Uses current Unity APIs only - Rigidbody2D.linearVelocity rather than the obsolete .velocity, if velocity is touched at all.
notes: Do NOT wire this into SceneGenerator and do NOT copy any art in this task. Those are separate steps that need the art files present first, and SceneGenerator.cs is not in your allowlist.
Read Assets/GameFactory/Gameplay/Runner/GroundSpawner.cs first - it already solves the recycle-when-passed problem for ground tiles and the same idiom should be used here rather than a new one.
The camera is orthographic with orthographicSize 5 and follows the player on X only (CameraFollow2D).

2026-09-05 REVIEWED BY CLAUDE, read line by line against the seven acceptance criteria - all seven met. SetLayers caches transforms, sprite widths and starting X at edit time; Configure takes only the numbers; Update allocates nothing and does no GetComponent; the wrap handles both scroll directions and is bounded because a layer with width <= 0 is skipped; with no layers assigned it returns silently and logs nothing; no UnityEditor reference; velocity is never touched. Two honest limits: NOT COMPILED here, and layerWidths are measured from lossyScale at edit time, so a layer whose parent is rescaled at runtime would wrap at the old width - fine for a fixed background, worth knowing.

STILL REVIEW because nothing uses it yet: SceneGenerator never calls SetLayers, so no generated scene has a background. That is correct for this task - its allowlist was the one .cs file - but the parallax is invisible in the game until CODEX-BGWIRE1 below builds the layer objects and wires them.

tasks.title: Three bugs in the board runner, found by running it for real
tasks.goal: The first real `team run` reported CODEX-ART1 as BLOCKED even though Codex had done the work correctly. Three separate defects in teamwork.py caused or contributed to that, all of them mine. Fix all three.
acceptance: (1) TOOL CHURN MUST NOT BLOCK A TASK. Packages/packages-lock.json is tracked, is not gitignored, and Unity rewrites it whenever the editor re-resolves packages. It changed during the run, so it landed in `after - before`, matched no allowlist, and blocked the task. Add a module-level tuple of paths that are regenerated by tools rather than authored by an agent - Packages/packages-lock.json at minimum - and exclude them from the outside-allowlist check. Report them separately in TaskRun instead of dropping them silently, so a real change there is still visible.

(2) save() MUST NOT CLOBBER HAND-EDITED FIELDS. It hardcodes _comment and _version into the payload on every write, so a comment edited by hand in the JSON is silently reverted the first time run_task saves. Preserve unknown top-level keys and any existing _comment; only write the default when the file had none. A board that cannot be annotated by hand is not the shared, human-readable handoff it is supposed to be.

(3) The concurrent-work warning in build_prompt should track the tree, not the status field. It currently names every in_progress/review task as 'being edited right now', which for already-committed work is false and warns Codex off stable files. List a task only when at least one of its declared files is actually dirty, and name those files. Reuse the existing changed_paths() helper and Task.covers() rather than adding new matching logic.
build_prompt keeps working when git is unavailable or the path is not a repo: fall back to the status-based behaviour rather than raising. A prompt builder must not be able to fail the run.

Tests for each: a tool-churn path does not block a task while a real stray file still does; a hand-edited _comment survives a save/load round trip; a committed REVIEW task is omitted from the warning while a dirty one is included with its filenames; and the no-git fallback.
Existing tests in test_teamwork.py still pass - test_the_prompt_warns_about_concurrent_work may need its fixture to dirty a file rather than only set a status.
notes: Read teamwork.py fully first. changed_paths() already handles renames and untracked files, and Task.covers() already matches a path against a task's allowlist patterns.
Keep it cheap: build_prompt runs once per run, so one git call is fine, but do not call git once per task.

Do NOT gitignore Packages/packages-lock.json to make the symptom go away. Unity projects are supposed to commit it so package versions stay pinned; the fix is that the allowlist check should know the difference between a tool regenerating a file and an agent editing one.

A SPEC-WRITING RULE worth keeping, recorded here because _comment gets overwritten until defect (2) is fixed: when a task edits a GENERATOR, the generator's committed OUTPUT belongs in that task's allowlist too, or verifying the change reads as going out of bounds. That is why Reports/dashboard.html is listed on CODEX-OFFICE1.

2026-09-03: DONE BY CLAUDE, not Codex, in the same pass. (1) TOOL_OWNED_PATHS tuple with Packages/packages-lock.json; run_task splits tool churn out of the diff before the allowlist check and reports it on TaskRun.tool_churn, which main.py prints separately. (2) TaskBoard keeps every non-'tasks' top-level key in .meta and save() writes them back, defaulting _comment/_version only when absent - so the note above about _comment being overwritten is now history. (3) concurrent_work() lists another agent's task only when one of its declared files is dirty, names the files, and falls back to the status-based reading when git cannot answer. build_prompt takes an optional repo_root; run_task and the dry-run pass it. 8 new tests; the pre-existing concurrent-work test still passes unchanged because it exercises the fallback.
REVIEW, not DONE: the tool-churn path has not yet been exercised by a real run with the Unity Editor open, which is the exact condition that produced the false BLOCKED on CODEX-ART1.

tasks.title: orchestrator test - run the Unity test suites locally
tasks.goal: There is no way to run the Unity tests from the orchestrator. run_pipeline deliberately does generate/validate/build and leaves tests to the workflow, but the self-hosted runner is not always up, and a task like CODEX-TEST1 that WRITES tests cannot be verified without running them. PlayMode test assemblies are also excluded from a player build, so `orchestrator build` does not even compile them - a syntax error in a test file passes the build and is caught by nobody. Add the missing step.
acceptance: UnityRunner gains a test step per platform, invoked exactly the way .github/workflows/test.yml already invokes it: wait-for-unity.ps1 with -TestResultsPath, and Unity args -batchmode -nographics -projectPath <repo> -runTests -testPlatform EditMode|PlayMode -testResults <xml> -logFile <log>. Do not invent flags; copy the ones the workflow proves work.
A new CLI command `orchestrator test` with --platform editmode|playmode|both (default both) and --game (default game01).
PlayMode tests load the generated scene in [UnitySetUp], so the command generates it first - reuse UnityRunner.generate(game_id) rather than duplicating the invocation.

It PARSES the NUnit XML result file and prints passed/failed/skipped counts plus the name and message of each failure. A test run whose XML is missing or unparsable is reported as a failure, never as a pass - same rule as verify_build.
Exit code 0 only when the XML exists AND reports zero failures. Section 38: 'Unity exited 0' is not 'the tests passed'.

Tests use the injected runner seam already in test_unity_runner.py: assert the emitted flags match the workflow's, that a missing XML fails, that a failing XML fails with the test names, and that a passing XML passes.
notes: Read unity_runner.py fully first. It already has the sentinel/exitcode handling, the timeout budget, and _run_powershell - the new step is another _step call, not new plumbing.

wait-for-unity.ps1 reads the editor path from $env:UNITY_PATH, which unity_runner already exports. Only ONE of -SentinelName/-TestResultsPath/-CompileLogPath is required, and the test steps in test.yml pass -TestResultsPath - that is sufficient and is the pattern to follow.
Do not change .github/workflows/test.yml. It works, and it is not in your allowlist.

2026-09-05 RUN + REVIEWED BY CLAUDE. Codex wrote all three allowlisted files and the work is sound. The point of the task is met exactly: _apply_test_results parses the NUnit XML and makes IT authoritative - a missing or unparsable XML is a failure, ok requires exit 0 AND failed == 0, and each failing test is named with its message. `orchestrator test --platform editmode|playmode|both` generates the scene first, stops if generation fails, and prints TESTS_FAILED rather than a bare exit code. Flags are the ones the workflow already proves work (-runTests -testPlatform -testResults); nothing was invented. test_unity_runner.py grew from 28 to 39 tests, all passing.

STILL REVIEW, and one thing is unverified for an honest reason: no run record exists for this task, so the run's own ending was never recorded - the code is complete but nobody has watched `orchestrator test` drive a real Unity. Running it once on the PC is the check, and it is also the first chance to see PlayMode results without the GitHub runner.

tasks.title: A start button on every waiting task, not one dropdown
tasks.goal: The control panel can already run a Codex task, but only through a single <select> of task ids. Put the button on the task itself: every waiting row in the 공유 작업판 section gets its own start button, so you press the thing you are looking at instead of matching an id in a dropdown.
acceptance: Each task row in the board section gets a start button when the page is SERVED, and none at all in the static file - a control with no server to POST to is worse than an absent one, and there is already a test asserting the static page has no control panel.

The button posts the SAME action the dropdown does: {action: 'team-run', arg: <task id>} to /run with the token. Reuse the existing start()/watch()/lock() functions in the injected script - do not write a second fetch/poll implementation.
Label: '작업 시작' for a todo task, '다시 실행' for in_progress, blocked or review. NO button on a done task - there is nothing left to run.
Only Codex-owned tasks get a button. A claude-owned row gets none, because server.py's valid_arg refuses those and a button that always errors is a lie about what the page can do.
A task with unmet dependencies renders its button DISABLED with the blocking task ids visible, since run_task refuses it anyway. board.unmet_dependencies() already computes this.

The existing lock() disables every .btn[data-act] while a job runs, so the new buttons must carry that same attribute shape and be disabled together - two jobs at once would fight over one working tree.
The dropdown may stay or go, your call, but if it goes the game/build combo and the ghost buttons must keep working.
Tests: a served page contains a start button per runnable Codex task and none for claude-owned or done tasks; the static page contains none; a task with an unmet dependency renders as disabled.
Regenerate Reports/dashboard.html and leave it in the working tree - it is in your allowlist for that reason, and it is the only evidence the section still renders.
notes: Read dashboard.py fully first. _control_html() builds the panel and holds the script; the board rows are built in render() near the 'lanes' list. The button markup belongs with the rows, the script stays in _control_html - so render() needs to know whether a token is present, which it already does.

tasks.title: Every orchestrator run leaves a committed log, so failures reach Claude without copy-paste
tasks.goal: Unity compile errors and build results already reach Claude on their own: sync-and-run.ps1 commits Reports/errors/latest.txt and Reports/build-status/latest.txt every 15 minutes and Claude reads them from the fork. Orchestrator runs have no such channel - when `team run` or `serve` or `codex --doctor` fails, the output dies on the PC console and the human has to retype it into a chat window. Three separate bugs on 2026-09-02 (WinError 2, a cp949 UnicodeDecodeError, and CODEX_LIMITED discarding a finished run) were all diagnosed that way. Apply the pattern that already works to the orchestrator.
acceptance: A new module company/orchestrator/runlog.py writes one file per orchestrator run under Reports/runs/, plus Reports/runs/latest.txt holding the most recent one. Follow the shape of the two files that already work - read Reports/errors/latest.txt and Reports/build-status/latest.txt first and match their heading style, because Claude parses those and a third format is a third parser.

Each entry records: UTC timestamp, the subcommand and its arguments, the exit code, how long it took, and the tail of stdout/stderr (cap the tail - a Unity build log must not land in git). A run that raised records the exception type and message.
It records FAILURES as loudly as successes. A run that ends non-zero, raises, or times out is the entire point of this task; a log that only contains successes is worse than none.
main.py wires it into every subcommand through ONE place, not by editing each cmd_* function. The dispatcher already calls args.func(args) - wrap that call.

SECRETS: no value of any key in policy blocked_env_keys, and no value of the env var named by gemini_api_key_env, may ever be written. Reuse the existing 'names only' idiom - CodexRunner.stripped_keys - do not write a second redaction path that can drift from it. A test asserts a key value placed in the environment does not appear in the written file.
The log directory is bounded: keep at most 50 entries, delete the oldest beyond that. This is committed to git, so unbounded growth is a repository problem, not just a disk one.

sync-and-run.ps1 commits Reports/runs/ alongside the two reports it already commits. It must stay ASCII-only - Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less UTF-8 .ps1 in the local codepage and Korean literals break parsing. That is not a style preference, it has already broken this exact file once.

Writing the log NEVER changes the outcome of the command. If the log cannot be written (read-only disk, missing directory, permission error), the run still returns its real exit code and the failure to log is reported on stderr and nowhere else. A logging bug that turns a passing build into a failure would be worse than the problem this task solves.

Tests: a successful run writes an entry; a non-zero run writes one saying so; a raising run writes one naming the exception; a secret in the environment never appears in the file; the 50-entry cap evicts oldest-first; a write failure does not change the returned exit code.
notes: WHY THIS EXISTS, in the user's words on 2026-09-02: '왜 gpt 실행해서 오류 나면 너한테 복사해서 붙이라고 하지? 혼자서 스스로 고치지 못해?' The answer is that Claude runs in a remote container with no access to the build PC, and the only channel between that console and Claude is a committed file. Unity already has that channel. The orchestrator does not. This closes it.

READ FIRST: scripts/dev/collect-errors.ps1 and scripts/dev/report-build-status.ps1 for the report format, and scripts/desktop/sync-and-run.ps1 lines 120-145 for how those two get committed. Do not invent a new mechanism next to a working one.

ALLOWLIST WARNING, learned the hard way: Reports/runs/* is in your allowlist because running the orchestrator to test your own change WRITES there, and the allowlist check reads `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`. Without it listed, testing your work correctly would be reported as going out of bounds and the task would come back BLOCKED. See CODEX-BOARD1.

This does not make the loop fully autonomous and should not pretend to. Claude still cannot press the button - the run has to be started on the PC. What it removes is the human retyping an error message. The remaining gap (starting a run without a human) is a separate decision about running Codex from the self-hosted Actions runner, and is not in scope here.
Do not log prompts sent to Codex. They can be long, they are reconstructable from the board, and the run log is meant to be read at a glance.

Values of every blocked_env_keys entry and of gemini_api_key_env are replaced with [REDACTED:<NAME>] before writing - tested with a fake key on both the stdout path and the exception path. A write failure is printed to stderr and never changes the exit code - tested with a file where the directory should be. tasks.title: Generate the parallax background layers and wire them into the scene
tasks.goal: CODEX-BG1 delivered ParallaxBackground.cs and it is sound, but nothing calls SetLayers, so every generated scene still has an empty sky. Build the layer objects at generation time from the CC0 background art already staged and approved, and wire them to the component.
acceptance: SceneGenerator creates N background layer GameObjects under the camera-facing root, each holding enough adjacent sprite copies to cover more than one screen width so the wrap is never visible at the edge.

It calls SetLayers with those transforms at generation time and Configure with the speed factors at runtime - the same edit-time/runtime split ParallaxBackground already implements. Do not put numbers in SetLayers or references in Configure.

Speed factors come from the GameSpec, not from a literal in the generator: distant layers slower than near ones. Add the field to GameSpecData/GameSpecValidator/docs/GAME_SPEC.md if it is not there, and default it so an existing spec without it still generates.
Art comes from kenney-background-elements-remastered, which is APPROVED in LICENSE_REGISTRY.json. Add targets to art-mapping.json; do NOT copy image files - apply-art-mapping.ps1 does that on the PC.
A scene generated for a spec with no background configured is UNCHANGED - no empty layer objects, no component added. The feature must be additive.
Sorting order puts every background layer behind the ground, the player and the obstacles.
Editor script: it may use UnityEditor. ParallaxBackground.cs itself is runtime and must NOT be edited here - it is finished and reviewed.
notes: Read Assets/GameFactory/Gameplay/Runner/ParallaxBackground.cs first - its SetLayers expects one Transform per layer, each with a SpriteRenderer somewhere beneath it that defines the repeat width.
The camera is orthographic, size 5, and follows the player on X (CameraFollow2D). A layer must span more than the visible width at that size or the wrap shows.

Two packs are approved and only ONE should be used: kenney-background-elements-remastered (162 images, the newer one) or kenney-backgroundElements (125, the spare). Mixing the two looks worse than either.
Do not change ParallaxBackground.cs. If it genuinely needs a change, stop and say so in your final message rather than editing outside this allowlist.
